# Power calculation for one-sample t-test
# H0: μ = 0 vs H1: μ > 0 (one-sided, upper tail)
# Parameters:
# - n = 25 participants
# - effect size: mean increase = 0.2 units
# - SD = 0.5 units
# - alpha = 0.05

library(stats)

# Parameters
n <- 25
delta <- 0.2  # mean increase (effect size in original units)
sigma <- 0.5  # standard deviation
alpha <- 0.05

# Calculate Cohen's d (standardized effect size)
cohens_d <- delta / sigma

# For a one-sample t-test, the non-centrality parameter is:
# λ = δ√n / σ = (μ - μ0) * √n / σ
# where μ - μ0 is the true difference
ncp <- cohens_d * sqrt(n)

# Critical value for one-sided test at α = 0.05
# df = n - 1
df <- n - 1
t_critical <- qt(1 - alpha, df, lower.tail = TRUE)

# Power = P(t > t_critical | H1 is true)
# This is the cumulative distribution of the non-central t distribution
power <- pt(t_critical, df, ncp = ncp, lower.tail = FALSE)

cat("One-Sample t-Test Power Calculation\n")
cat("=====================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Sample size (n): %d participants\n", n))
cat(sprintf("Mean increase (δ): %.1f units\n", delta))
cat(sprintf("Standard deviation (σ): %.1f units\n", sigma))
cat(sprintf("Standardized effect size (Cohen's d): %.4f\n", cohens_d))
cat(sprintf("Non-centrality parameter (λ): %.4f\n", ncp))
cat(sprintf("Degrees of freedom: %d\n", df))
cat(sprintf("Critical t-value (one-sided, α=0.05): %.4f\n", t_critical))
cat(sprintf("Alpha (significance level): %.3f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("Power: %.6f\n", power))

# Store result for submission
power_value <- power

# Independent verification of one-sample t-test power calculation
# Parameters from candidate: n=25, δ=0.2, σ=0.5, α=0.05, one-sided (upper tail)

library(stats)

n <- 25
delta <- 0.2    # true mean increase
sigma <- 0.5    # standard deviation
alpha <- 0.05

# Method 1: Non-central t distribution (direct calculation)
# Under H1: true mean = 0.2
# Test statistic: t = (X̄ - 0) / (S/√n)
# Non-centrality parameter λ = (true_mean - null_mean) * √n / σ
#                             = 0.2 * √25 / 0.5 = 2.0

ncp <- delta * sqrt(n) / sigma
df <- n - 1
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)  # one-sided upper tail critical value

# Power = P(t_{24} > t_crit | H1), where t_{24} ~ t(df=24, ncp=λ)
power_direct <- pt(t_crit, df, ncp = ncp, lower.tail = FALSE)

cat("=== Independent Verification ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Non-centrality parameter (λ): %.6f\n", ncp))
cat(sprintf("Critical t-value (df=24, α=0.05, one-sided): %.6f\n", t_crit))
cat(sprintf("Power (pt method): %.6f\n", power_direct))

# Method 2: Using pwr package for cross-check
library(pwr)
cohens_d <- delta / sigma
result_pwr <- pwr.t.test(n = n, d = cohens_d, sig.level = alpha, 
                          alternative = "greater", type = "one.sample")

cat(sprintf("Power (pwr package): %.6f\n", result_pwr$power))

# Method 3: Monte Carlo simulation (pilot with 10,000 replicates)
set.seed(42)
nsim <- 10000
test_stats <- numeric(nsim)

for (i in 1:nsim) {
  # Generate data under H1: Y ~ N(0.2, 0.5)
  y <- rnorm(n, mean = delta, sd = sigma)
  test_stats[i] <- mean(y) / (sd(y) / sqrt(n))
}

# Power = proportion of |t| > t_crit for one-sided upper tail
power_mc <- mean(test_stats > t_crit)
se_mc <- sqrt(power_mc * (1 - power_mc) / nsim)

cat(sprintf("\nMonte Carlo validation (10,000 simulations):\n"))
cat(sprintf("Power (MC): %.6f (SE: %.6f)\n", power_mc, se_mc))
cat(sprintf("95%% CI: [%.6f, %.6f]\n", 
            power_mc - 1.96*se_mc, power_mc + 1.96*se_mc))

# Summary table
cat("\n=== Summary of Results ===\n")
cat(sprintf("%-30s %10.6f\n", "Direct (non-central t):", power_direct))
cat(sprintf("%-30s %10.6f\n", "pwr package:", result_pwr$power))
cat(sprintf("%-30s %10.6f\n", "Monte Carlo (n_sim=10000):", power_mc))

# Final result
final_power <- power_direct
cat(sprintf("\nFinal Power: %.6f\n", final_power))

POWER_AGENT_RESULT=jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(results = list(
    list(metric = "power", value = final_power, unit = "probability")
  )),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)

# Power calculation for one-sample t-test
# H0: μ = 0 vs H1: μ > 0 (one-sided, upper tail)
# Parameters:
# - n = 25 participants
# - effect size: mean increase = 0.2 units
# - SD = 0.5 units
# - alpha = 0.05

library(stats)

# Parameters
n <- 25
delta <- 0.2  # mean increase (effect size in original units)
sigma <- 0.5  # standard deviation
alpha <- 0.05

# Calculate Cohen's d (standardized effect size)
cohens_d <- delta / sigma

# For a one-sample t-test, the non-centrality parameter is:
# λ = δ√n / σ = (μ - μ0) * √n / σ
# where μ - μ0 is the true difference
ncp <- cohens_d * sqrt(n)

# Critical value for one-sided test at α = 0.05
# df = n - 1
df <- n - 1
t_critical <- qt(1 - alpha, df, lower.tail = TRUE)

# Power = P(t > t_critical | H1 is true)
# This is the cumulative distribution of the non-central t distribution
power <- pt(t_critical, df, ncp = ncp, lower.tail = FALSE)

cat("One-Sample t-Test Power Calculation\n")
cat("=====================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Sample size (n): %d participants\n", n))
cat(sprintf("Mean increase (δ): %.1f units\n", delta))
cat(sprintf("Standard deviation (σ): %.1f units\n", sigma))
cat(sprintf("Standardized effect size (Cohen's d): %.4f\n", cohens_d))
cat(sprintf("Non-centrality parameter (λ): %.4f\n", ncp))
cat(sprintf("Degrees of freedom: %d\n", df))
cat(sprintf("Critical t-value (one-sided, α=0.05): %.4f\n", t_critical))
cat(sprintf("Alpha (significance level): %.3f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("Power: %.6f\n", power))

# Independent verification of one-sample t-test power calculation
# Parameters from candidate: n=25, δ=0.2, σ=0.5, α=0.05, one-sided (upper tail)

library(stats)

n <- 25
delta <- 0.2    # true mean increase
sigma <- 0.5    # standard deviation
alpha <- 0.05

# Method 1: Non-central t distribution (direct calculation)
# Under H1: true mean = 0.2
# Test statistic: t = (X̄ - 0) / (S/√n)
# Non-centrality parameter λ = (true_mean - null_mean) * √n / σ
#                             = 0.2 * √25 / 0.5 = 2.0

ncp <- delta * sqrt(n) / sigma
df <- n - 1
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)  # one-sided upper tail critical value

# Power = P(t_{24} > t_crit | H1), where t_{24} ~ t(df=24, ncp=λ)
power_direct <- pt(t_crit, df, ncp = ncp, lower.tail = FALSE)

cat("=== Independent Verification ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Non-centrality parameter (λ): %.6f\n", ncp))
cat(sprintf("Critical t-value (df=24, α=0.05, one-sided): %.6f\n", t_crit))
cat(sprintf("Power (pt method): %.6f\n", power_direct))

# Method 2: Using pwr package for cross-check
library(pwr)
cohens_d <- delta / sigma
result_pwr <- pwr.t.test(n = n, d = cohens_d, sig.level = alpha, 
                          alternative = "greater", type = "one.sample")

cat(sprintf("Power (pwr package): %.6f\n", result_pwr$power))

# Method 3: Monte Carlo simulation (pilot with 10,000 replicates)
set.seed(42)
nsim <- 10000
test_stats <- numeric(nsim)

for (i in 1:nsim) {
  # Generate data under H1: Y ~ N(0.2, 0.5)
  y <- rnorm(n, mean = delta, sd = sigma)
  test_stats[i] <- mean(y) / (sd(y) / sqrt(n))
}

# Power = proportion of |t| > t_crit for one-sided upper tail
power_mc <- mean(test_stats > t_crit)
se_mc <- sqrt(power_mc * (1 - power_mc) / nsim)

cat(sprintf("\nMonte Carlo validation (10,000 simulations):\n"))
cat(sprintf("Power (MC): %.6f (SE: %.6f)\n", power_mc, se_mc))
cat(sprintf("95%% CI: [%.6f, %.6f]\n", 
            power_mc - 1.96*se_mc, power_mc + 1.96*se_mc))

# Summary table
cat("\n=== Summary of Results ===\n")
cat(sprintf("%-30s %10.6f\n", "Direct (non-central t):", power_direct))
cat(sprintf("%-30s %10.6f\n", "pwr package:", result_pwr$power))
cat(sprintf("%-30s %10.6f\n", "Monte Carlo (n_sim=10000):", power_mc))

final_power <- power_direct
cat(sprintf("\nFinal Power: %.6f\n", final_power))

# Evidence e1; success=true

# Power calculation for one-sample t-test
# H0: μ = 0 vs H1: μ > 0 (one-sided, upper tail)
# Parameters:
# - n = 25 participants
# - effect size: mean increase = 0.2 units
# - SD = 0.5 units
# - alpha = 0.05

library(stats)

# Parameters
n <- 25
delta <- 0.2  # mean increase (effect size in original units)
sigma <- 0.5  # standard deviation
alpha <- 0.05

# Calculate Cohen's d (standardized effect size)
cohens_d <- delta / sigma

# For a one-sample t-test, the non-centrality parameter is:
# λ = δ√n / σ = (μ - μ0) * √n / σ
# where μ - μ0 is the true difference
ncp <- cohens_d * sqrt(n)

# Critical value for one-sided test at α = 0.05
# df = n - 1
df <- n - 1
t_critical <- qt(1 - alpha, df, lower.tail = TRUE)

# Power = P(t > t_critical | H1 is true)
# This is the cumulative distribution of the non-central t distribution
power <- pt(t_critical, df, ncp = ncp, lower.tail = FALSE)

cat("One-Sample t-Test Power Calculation\n")
cat("=====================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Sample size (n): %d participants\n", n))
cat(sprintf("Mean increase (δ): %.1f units\n", delta))
cat(sprintf("Standard deviation (σ): %.1f units\n", sigma))
cat(sprintf("Standardized effect size (Cohen's d): %.4f\n", cohens_d))
cat(sprintf("Non-centrality parameter (λ): %.4f\n", ncp))
cat(sprintf("Degrees of freedom: %d\n", df))
cat(sprintf("Critical t-value (one-sided, α=0.05): %.4f\n", t_critical))
cat(sprintf("Alpha (significance level): %.3f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("Power: %.6f\n", power))

# Store result for submission
power_value <- power


# Evidence e2; success=true

# Verification using the pwr package
library(pwr)

# For one-sample t-test in pwr package:
# - d = Cohen's d (effect size)
# - n = sample size
# - sig.level = α
# - alternative = "greater" for one-sided upper tail

n <- 25
d <- 0.2 / 0.5  # Cohen's d = 0.4
alpha <- 0.05

# Calculate power
result <- pwr.t.test(n = n, d = d, sig.level = alpha, 
                      alternative = "greater", type = "one.sample")

cat("Verification using pwr package:\n")
cat("================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Power (from pwr): %.6f\n", result$power))

# Also report with more decimal places
power_verified <- result$power
cat(sprintf("Power (maximum precision): %.15f\n", power_verified))

# Comparison
cat("\nComparison of methods:\n")
cat(sprintf("Direct calculation: %.6f\n", 0.617259))
cat(sprintf("pwr package:        %.6f\n", power_verified))


# Evidence e3; success=true

# Final power calculation with POWER_AGENT_RESULT output
library(pwr)

n <- 25
d <- 0.2 / 0.5  # Cohen's d
alpha <- 0.05

result <- pwr.t.test(n = n, d = d, sig.level = alpha, 
                      alternative = "greater", type = "one.sample")

power <- result$power

# Emit structured result
